title: Offline mode and reconnection behaviour
goal: Make the client behave sensibly when the network or backend is unavailable: queue outgoing session frames safely, show honest connection states, resume cleanly, and never block local or LAN work because the backend is down.
scope_in: Connectivity monitor combining RelayClient link state, HTTP transport errors and `GET /v1/status` (cached 15 s) into one `NetState`: `online | reconnecting | offline | degraded | backend-down` and maps it to the client-local state names `online`, `reconnecting`, `offline` for the mascot/status line.

Durable outbox for session frames that were created while disconnected: bounded on-disk store per session (max 500 frames and 4 MiB, oldest-first refusal with a user-visible `OfflineBufferFull`), preserving ids so the C055 de-dup makes replay safe; flushed in order after `welcome`.

Resume orchestration glue for CT-RESUME on the client: choose hot-buffer resume vs snapshot restore from `sys.resumed`, persist `lastSeq` per session (a `SeqStore` for C055), show 'earlier history unavailable' when history is incomplete, never discard unsent frames.
Cached entitlements/flags/status used offline per CT-ENTITLEMENTS §6 (display up to 24 h) via reading the other clients' caches through injected getters.

Offline policies: LAN and local sessions stay fully functional; hosted-only actions (create hosted session, join-token, usage upload) return a typed `OfflineError` quickly (<= 1 s) rather than hanging; token refresh retries in the background with backoff.
Wake-from-sleep handling: on a timer gap > 30 s assume dead sockets, force-reconnect all relay clients with jitter 0-2 s to avoid thundering herd.
scope_out: Socket reconnect internals: lane C054. Ordering and acks: lane C055. Local session persistence/resume of transcripts: lane C026.
Usage event buffering: lane C065. Entitlement cache logic: lane C064.
Offline UI components (banners, toasts): TUI lanes.
build_against: the mock backend (lane C007): REST from OpenAPI plus the WebSocket relay simulator, started in-process with `startMockBackend()` from @centcom/testkit; no real backend is needed. The mock can be paused, killed and restarted (`mock.pause()`, `mock.stop()`, `mock.start()`), made to answer 503 on /readyz-class paths, and to purge its hot buffer to force `snapshot_required`. Local persistence (lane C026) is replaced by a temp-dir store.
interfaces: `new NetStateMonitor(o: { relays: () => RelayClient[]; http: HttpClient; clock; pollStatusMs?: number /*15000*/ })`; `current(): NetState`; `on('change', (s: NetState, prev: NetState) => void)`; `toMascotState(s: NetState): 'online'|'reconnecting'|'offline'`

`createDurableOutbox(dir: string, sid: string, o?: { maxFrames?: number /*500*/; maxBytes?: number /*4194304*/ }): DurableOutbox` with `push(draft): Promise<void>`, `drain(channel: ReliableChannel): Promise<number>`, `size(): { frames: number; bytes: number }`, `clear()`
`class ResumeCoordinator { constructor(o: { channel: ReliableChannel; session: SessionHandle; seqStore: SeqStore }); on('history-incomplete', fn); on('restored', fn) }`
`requireOnline<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>, o?: { timeoutMs?: number /*1000*/ }): Promise<T>` throwing `OfflineError`
acceptance: Killing the mock for 60 s: NetState goes `online` -> `reconnecting` (within 1 s of the close) -> `offline` after the second failed attempt; restarting the mock returns to `online` within 15 s and the status-line mapping emits `offline` then `online` events once each.

Frames created while offline (10) are stored in order, survive a process restart (new DurableOutbox instance on the same dir), and after reconnect reach the mock exactly once each with their original ids; the order at the mock equals creation order.
The 501st frame or the byte cap is refused with `OfflineBufferFull`; nothing already stored is dropped.

Forcing `snapshot_required` (mock hot buffer purged) results in snapshot restore then history catch-up; if the mock has no snapshot and history starts after our lastSeq+1, `history-incomplete` fires once and the session continues from the earliest retained frame.
A hosted action (`createSession`) with the mock stopped fails with OfflineError in <= 1 s; a LAN session start and a local agent run succeed with the mock stopped (no network calls observed).
`/v1/status` reporting `partial_outage` yields NetState `degraded` (banner) but does not close any open socket or block any command.
Simulating a 45 s timer gap (fake clock jump) triggers a forced reconnect of every open RelayClient within 2 s + jitter, each with a fresh ticket.
SeqStore persistence: after restart the first hello carries the persisted `last_seq` and the mock replays only frames after it.
Cached entitlements are reported as usable for display for 24 h offline and `stale:true` afterwards; hosted-action gating is never decided by this stale cache alone.
A frame buffered offline under `k1` is sent after reconnect under `k2` when a `control.rotate_key` arrived meanwhile; its `id` is unchanged and the mock decrypts it with the `k2` key.
tests: offline/net-state.test.ts: transitions with the mock killed/paused/degraded; mapping to mascot states.
offline/outbox-store.test.ts: persistence, order, caps, corruption recovery (truncated file ignored with warning).
offline/wake-detector.test.ts: gap detection and jitter spread.
offline/lan-unaffected.test.ts: asserts zero outbound HTTP/WS to the mock while running a LAN/local scenario with the backend down.
offline/failure-injection.test.ts: seeded chaos (random kills, delays) keeps exactly-once at the mock.
guardrails: MUST NOT block, delay or fail LAN or local-only functionality because the backend is down, degraded or unreachable (ARCHITECTURE §5; CT-STATUS).
MUST NOT store plaintext message bodies in the durable outbox: store the already-encrypted-and-signed frame (ciphertext) only, with file mode 0600, and never log its contents.

MUST keep frame ids unchanged across restarts so server de-dup holds; a frame that was already transmitted MUST be resent byte-identical, and only never-sent frames may be (re-)encrypted. Outbox payloads at rest MUST be encrypted with a device-local key from the OS keychain.
MUST bound the outbox (500 frames / 4 MiB per session) and refuse loudly rather than evict silently.
MUST NOT replay stored frames after the session ended or the member was removed (4403/4404): discard and tell the user.
MUST NOT spin: reconnect scheduling is owned by C054's backoff; this lane only observes and coordinates.
failure_modes: Corrupt or truncated outbox file -> ignore the damaged tail, keep the valid prefix, warn once.

Key epoch rotated while frames are buffered offline -> never-sent frames are re-encrypted under the current epoch (fresh nonce and signature, same frame id) when sent; already-transmitted frames are resent byte-identical.
Disk full or unwritable state dir -> offline buffering disabled with a warning; the live path is unaffected.
Status endpoint unreachable but relay connected -> NetState stays `online` (status is advisory).
notes: G2 checks 'resume survives a forced disconnect'; the acceptance items on forced disconnect and snapshot restore are the ones the gate script will run.
